title: AWS Marketplace Private Offer Errors: Why a Buyer Can't Accept
summary: Why a buyer can't accept your AWS Marketplace private offer: the 404, active-contract and payment errors, who fixes each one, and when a new offer helps.
body_markdown:
*When a buyer can’t accept an AWS Marketplace private offer, the error names what broke, and what broke decides who fixes it. A new offer is the right fix for only a few of them.*


---


The buyer opens the link and sends back an error. The reflex is to cancel the offer and send another. **That fixes a targeting mistake and little else.** A second offer to an account that already holds a contract can hit the same error or, on a product with Concurrent Agreements, become a second contract. After a declined card, the original link works once the payment is fixed. Read the error first.


## Which error is it, and who fixes it?


**Each acceptance failure has one owner: the buyer, their AWS administrator, their finance team, or you.** Route it there before anyone rebuilds anything.


What you see Likely cause Owner Fix


Page not found (404) on the offer link Signed in to another AWS account, or opened the link before signing in Buyer Sign in to the account on the offer, then open the link


A 404, with the offer under **Accepted and expired offers** It expired at 23:59:59 UTC on its expiry date You Extend the expiry; rebuild only if AWS refuses


A 404 on the right account, AMI product A limited listing that hasn’t allow-listed the account You (single AMI) or AWS’s Private Offer Success Team Allow-list the account, once per product


A 404 on the right account, any product The user lacks` aws-marketplace:ViewSubscriptions` Buyer’s AWS administrator Grant a Marketplace buyer policy


Product not available in their private catalog Their private marketplace excludes it Buyer’s private marketplace administrator Add it to their allow list


”You already have an active contract” The account already holds an agreement for the product You Amend that agreement


Acceptance email, then at once a cancellation email No permission to buy, a declined card or payment setup, or an unpaid AWS bill Buyer’s administrator or finance team Fix it, then accept the same offer again


Wrong account ID, or a buyer outside the offer’s countries Targeting is fixed at release You Clone, correct, cancel the original


A 404 that survives every row gets AWS’s browser checklist (sign out and back in, clear the cache and cookies, try another browser), then the Private Offer Success Team.


## What does “You already have an active contract” mean?


**The buyer’s account already holds an active subscription to the product, and the product allows only one.** That is AWS’s rule for SaaS contract and contract-with-consumption products, so a second offer to the same account meets the same wall.


**An agreement-based offer is** a private offer built on the existing agreement that replaces it when the buyer accepts. In Suger, open the buyer’s entitlement and choose **Upsell / Renew** . AWS says to “include any pending payment terms from the original offer in the agreement-based offer, as it will override remaining payments not yet invoiced”; if the buyer lets it expire, “the original agreement will continue unchanged.” On a channel partner deal, the partner builds it from a new selling authorization you grant.[What an amendment replaces, and what it can’t change](https://www.suger.io/resources/blog/co-terming-and-expanding-marketplace-agreements/) covers the pricing.


Other product types take other routes:


- **AMI hourly and annual:** a new offer overrides the old terms on acceptance, but “pending charges from the previous offer’s payment schedule will continue unless cancelled.”
- **AMI contracts:** cancel the current subscription first, through AWS’s refund and cancellation form. For SaaS, that form is the heavier alternative to amending.
- **Professional services:** AWS’s FAQ still says cancel first, but AWS switched on Concurrent Agreements for every Professional Services listing on February 26, 2026. Ask AWS before cancelling anything.


**Concurrent Agreements is** AWS’s option for one buyer account to hold several active agreements for the same product: the default for SaaS listings created after June 1, 2026, and opt-in for older ones. Buyers there “can accept multiple offers for the same product without disrupting existing agreements,” so the error should not appear, and a second offer sits beside the first rather than replacing it. If the deal is a replacement, amend.


## Can you extend an expired private offer?


**Usually, yes.** AWS lets you update an expired offer’s expiration date, which returns it to **Active** . In Suger, **More actions → Extend Expiry Date** works on` Pending_Acceptance` ,` Expired` and` Update_Failed` offers, with a new date later than the current one.


The payment schedule is the limit. Only one charge date may fall on or before the expiration, and a released offer takes a new expiration only if it still fits the schedule, so an extension past a second installment date is refused.


Suger shows the refusal on the offer: the status` Update_Failed` , an **Update Offer Failed** alert quoting AWS’s reason, and a **Why AWS rejected this** panel under **More actions → History** (and on the Offers page’s **Logs** tab) with AWS’s error code and message and up to three recent attempts. The fix is then a new offer, with the installments moved so no more than one falls on or before the new expiry.


## When does a new offer actually fix it?


**When the offer was aimed at the wrong target.** AWS’s Catalog API refuses to add a buyer after release: “BuyerAccounts can’t be added after the offer is released.” Country targeting is the quieter version: a buyer outside the offer’s selected countries cannot accept, and a linked account is judged by its own location, not the payer account’s.


Clone it. AWS’s clone flow offers **Cancel the existing offer** , which expires the original when the clone publishes without touching an accepted agreement. In Suger, **More actions → Clone** copies the product, SKUs and pricing, term dates, EULA and internal notes into a draft; correct the buyer ID and dates, send it, and cancel the original.


Check the carried-over dates. A past installment date is refused with “Provide a first charge date that isn’t in the past,” which through Suger reads “Failed to create offer: Offer PaymentTerms.Schedule.ChargeOn is not valid.” A failed clone sits in` Create_Failed` with **Edit** and **Submit** still available, so fix and resubmit that draft.[Diagnosing offers that fail to create](https://www.suger.io/resources/guides/ai-diagnose-offer-failures/) covers that side.


## Why does an accepted offer get cancelled straight away?


**An acceptance email followed at once by a cancellation email means the purchase failed on the buyer’s side.** Suger’s FAQ names three causes: the person accepting lacks permission to complete the transaction, the card was declined or the account isn’t set up for payment, or the buyer hasn’t paid their latest AWS bill.


The first two are likelier than they sound.` AWSMarketplaceRead-only` lets a user view private offers; subscribing takes a policy such as` AWSMarketplaceManageSubscriptions` . And a typical private offer is paid in full at acceptance unless financed, which is the kind of large charge card issuers often reject as possible fraud. Ask early whether the buyer pays AWS by invoice or by card.


Suger flags it with a` purchase_failed` sub-status: accepted, with the entitlements cancelled shortly after creation. No new offer is needed: once the cause is fixed, the buyer accepts the same offer from the same link.


## Frequently asked questions


### Why does my buyer get a 404 on an AWS private offer link?


Usually they opened the link while signed in to another AWS account, or before signing in. Otherwise the offer expired, an AMI limited listing has not allow-listed their account, or the user cannot view private offers.


### What does the active contract error on an AWS private offer mean?


The account already holds an active subscription to a product that allows only one. Amend that agreement with an agreement-based offer carrying its pending payments. A new offer to the same account gets the same error.


### Can a buyer accept the same AWS private offer again after a failed payment?


Yes. Suger documentation says the buyer can accept the same offer again, from the same link, once the permission, card, payment setup or unpaid AWS bill is fixed. No new offer is needed.


### Why was my AWS private offer expiry extension rejected?


Only one charge date may fall on or before the expiry, and a released offer takes a new expiry only if it fits the payment schedule. Past a second installment date, build a new offer instead.


### Can I change the buyer account ID on a released AWS private offer?


No. AWS does not allow buyer accounts to be added or removed once an offer is released. Clone it, correct the account ID and any past installment dates, and cancel the original.


## Takeaways


- Read the error first; each one has a single owner, and a 404 is usually the buyer’s sign-in.
- When the account already holds a contract, amend it and carry the pending payments. Don’t re-send.
- Extend an expired offer before rebuilding it; the payment schedule decides whether you can.
- Clone for a wrong account or country, and check the dates the clone copies.


The buyer’s half of the flow, from who signs in to who approves the spend, is in[what buyers see when you send a private offer](https://www.suger.io/resources/blog/what-buyers-see-when-you-send-a-private-offer/) . Suger’s[private offer management](https://www.suger.io/platform/private-offers/) keeps each offer’s status, history and AWS’s rejection reasons on the offer itself, the first place to look when a buyer says the link doesn’t work.
